title: ACT ON THE APPOINTMENT, ETC. OF A SPECIAL PROSECUTOR TO ASCERTAIN THE TRUTH CONCERNING OBSTRUCTION OF THE INVESTIGATION INTO A MARINE'S DEATH IN THE LINE OF DUTY AND CONCEALMENT OF THE CASE, ETC.
title_original: 순직 해병 수사 방해 및 사건 은폐 등의 진상규명을 위한 특별검사의 임명 등에 관한 법률
full_text:
ACT ON THE APPOINTMENT, ETC. OF A SPECIAL PROSECUTOR TO ASCERTAIN THE TRUTH CONCERNING OBSTRUCTION OF THE INVESTIGATION INTO A MARINE'S DEATH IN THE LINE OF DUTY AND CONCEALMENT OF THE CASE, ETC.

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to prescribe matters necessary for the appointment, duties, etc. of a Special Prosecutor with independent status to ascertain the truth concerning the cases specified in Article 2.

Article 2 (Matters Subject to Investigation by Special Prosecutor, etc.)
(1) Investigations by the Special Prosecutor under this Act shall be limited to the following cases and related cases:
1. The case concerning the death of Marine Chae Su-geun;
2. Dereliction of duty, abuse of official authority, and other unlawful acts related thereto involving former President Yoon Suk Yeol, the Office of the President, the Ministry of National Defense, Marine Corps Headquarters, the Gyeongbuk Provincial Police Agency, the National Human Rights Commission, etc., including concealment, suppression, inducements, and fabrication of the case in connection with subparagraph 1 (persons concerned with the case, including military judicial police, the military prosecution unit, military judge advocates, and the Military Human Rights Protector, shall be included among the subjects);
3. Unlawful acts relating to allegations of external pressure on the investigation by the Corruption Investigation Office for High-Ranking Officials in connection with subparagraph 2;
4. Unlawful acts in the process of former Minister of National Defense Lee Jong-seop's appointment as Ambassador to Australia, departure, return, and resignation;
5. Dereliction of duty, abuse of official authority, and related unlawful acts involving former President Yoon Suk Yeol, the Office of the President, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Justice, the Corruption Investigation Office for High-Ranking Officials, etc., including concealment, suppression, and inducements in connection with subparagraph 4;
6. The case of alleged illegal lobbying in which Lee Jong-ho and others asked Kim Keon-hee and others to secure protection for Lim Seong-geun in connection with the death of Marine Chae Su-geun;
7. The case of allegations that former President Yoon Suk Yeol and the Office of the President committed unlawful acts, including obstructing inquiries and investigations into the suspected cases related to subparagraphs 1 through 6;
8. Related cases discovered in the course of investigating the preceding subparagraphs.
(2) Public officials subject to investigation under paragraph (1) shall not obstruct or impede the Special Prosecutor's investigation and shall recuse themselves from performing the relevant duties where they determine that it is difficult to perform such duties impartially in connection with the investigation.
(3) In this Act, the term "related cases" means cases falling under any of the following subparagraphs: <Newly inserted on September 26, 2025>
1. Offenses of harboring offenders, destruction of evidence, perjury, false expert opinions or interpretation, or offenses concerning stolen property, and the underlying principal offenses;
2. Offenses sharing evidence secured pursuant to warrants in connection with the cases specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1);
3. Offenses under Articles 129 through 133, 355, and 356 of the Criminal Act that constitute the source of criminal proceeds in this case or arise from the disposition of such proceeds;
4. Offenses committed for a single purpose, concurrently or in a means-and-result relationship, in connection with the cases specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1);
5. Cases involving complaints or accusations related to suspected cases connected with paragraph (1) 1 through 7.

Article 3 (Appointment of Special Prosecutor)
(1) To investigate the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1), the Speaker of the National Assembly shall, within two days from the date this Act enters into force, request the President in writing to appoint one Special Prosecutor.
(2) Within two days from the date of receipt of the request under paragraph (1), the President shall request in writing that the Democratic Party of Korea, from among the negotiating blocs under Article 33 of the National Assembly Act, and the group holding the largest number of seats among groups that are not negotiating blocs recommend candidates for the appointment of one Special Prosecutor. If the President fails to make the request within two days, the Speaker of the National Assembly shall make it without delay.
(3) The Democratic Party of Korea and the group holding the largest number of seats among groups that are not negotiating blocs, upon receiving a request to recommend candidates for Special Prosecutor under paragraph (2), shall each recommend one person to the President in writing within five days from the date of receipt of the request, from among persons who have held the positions specified in the subparagraphs of Article 42 (1) of the Court Organization Act for at least 15 years (the periods of service of persons who have held two or more of the positions specified in the subparagraphs of Article 42 (1) of the Court Organization Act shall be aggregated).
(4) The President, upon receiving recommendations for two candidates for Special Prosecutor under paragraph (3), shall appoint one of the recommended candidates as Special Prosecutor within three days from the date of receipt of the recommendations.
(5) If the President fails to appoint a Special Prosecutor under paragraph (4), the older of the candidates recommended under paragraph (3) shall be deemed appointed as Special Prosecutor.

Article 4 (Grounds for Disqualification of Special Prosecutor)
A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall not be appointed as Special Prosecutor:
1. A person who is not a national of the Republic of Korea;
2. A public official under Article 2 of the State Public Officials Act or Article 2 of the Local Public Officials Act;
3. A person who held a position specified in subparagraph 2 within one year before the date of appointment as Special Prosecutor;
4. A person who is or has been a member of a political party;
5. A person who has registered as a candidate (including a preliminary candidate) in an election held under the Public Official Election Act;
6. A person falling under any subparagraph of Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act.

Article 5 (Political Neutrality and Independence in Performance of Duties of Special Prosecutor)
The Special Prosecutor shall maintain political neutrality and perform his or her duties independently.

Article 6 (Scope of Duties and Powers of Special Prosecutor, etc.)
(1) The scope of duties of the Special Prosecutor shall be as follows: <Amended on September 26, 2025>
1. Investigation of the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1), determination of whether to institute prosecution, and conduct of prosecution (in the case of conduct of prosecution, including determination of whether to withdraw prosecution in cases already on trial);
2. Direction and supervision of Assistant Special Prosecutors and Special Investigators appointed under Article 7 and public officials seconded from relevant agencies;
3. Direction of correctional officials for the execution of court warrants against persons detained in correctional facilities.
(2) The Special Prosecutor shall not exceed the scope of his or her duties by summoning or investigating persons unrelated to the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1).
(3) Where necessary in performing his or her duties, the Special Prosecutor may request cooperation in investigations from the heads of relevant agencies, including the Supreme Prosecutors' Office, the Corruption Investigation Office for High-Ranking Officials, the National Police Agency, and the Ministry of National Defense, including the submission of investigation records, evidence, and other materials concerning cases related to those specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1), and support for investigative activities, such as the provision of forensic equipment and facilities and expert assistance. <Amended on September 26, 2025>
(4) Where necessary in performing his or her duties, the Special Prosecutor may request the heads of relevant agencies, including the Supreme Prosecutors' Office, the Corruption Investigation Office for High-Ranking Officials, the National Police Agency, and the Ministry of National Defense, to second public officials under their jurisdiction and provide related support: Provided, That the number of seconded prosecutors shall not exceed 30, and the number of seconded public officials other than seconded prosecutors shall not exceed 60. <Amended on September 26, 2025>
(5) In connection with the secondment of public officials from relevant agencies under paragraph (4), at least one-tenth of all seconded personnel shall be seconded from the Corruption Investigation Office for High-Ranking Officials.
(6) The heads of relevant agencies receiving requests under paragraphs (3) and (4) shall comply with them. If the head of a relevant agency fails to comply, the Special Prosecutor may request the authority empowered to request a disciplinary decision to initiate disciplinary proceedings against that head.
(7) The provisions concerning the powers of prosecutors, military prosecutors, and prosecutors of the Corruption Investigation Office for High-Ranking Officials in the Criminal Procedure Act, the Prosecutors' Office Act (excluding Article 4 (2)), the Military Court Act, the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the Corruption Investigation Office for High-Ranking Officials, and other statutes and regulations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Special Prosecutor insofar as they do not conflict with this Act. <Amended on September 26, 2025>

Article 7 (Assistant Special Prosecutors, Special Investigators, etc.)
(1) The Special Prosecutor may select eight candidates for Assistant Special Prosecutor from among persons who have held the positions specified in the subparagraphs of Article 42 (1) of the Court Organization Act for at least seven years (for a person who has held two or more of those positions, the periods of service in those positions shall be aggregated) and request the President to appoint Assistant Special Prosecutors, and the President shall appoint four of those candidates as Assistant Special Prosecutors within three days from the date of receipt of the request. Where the President fails to appoint Assistant Special Prosecutors, Article 3 (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis.
(2) Assistant Special Prosecutors shall, under the direction and supervision of the Special Prosecutor, take charge of investigations relating to the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1) and the conduct of prosecution in cases in which prosecution has been instituted, and shall direct and supervise Special Investigators and public officials seconded from relevant agencies. Seconded prosecutors may conduct prosecution in court under the direction and supervision of the Special Prosecutor or an Assistant Special Prosecutor without the in-court presence of the Special Prosecutor or an Assistant Special Prosecutor. <Amended on September 26, 2025>
(3) Where necessary for the performance of duties, the Special Prosecutor may appoint not more than 50 Special Investigators. <Amended on September 26, 2025>
(4) Special Investigators shall perform the duties of judicial police officers within the scope of investigations of the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1).
(5) Article 4 shall apply mutatis mutandis to grounds for disqualification of Assistant Special Prosecutors and Special Investigators, and Article 6 (7) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the powers of Assistant Special Prosecutors, respectively.
(6) For the conduct of prosecution after completion of investigations, the Special Prosecutor shall maintain the number of persons assisting the Special Prosecutor in the performance of duties, including Assistant Special Prosecutors and Special Investigators, at the minimum necessary level.

Article 8 (Duties of the Special Prosecutor, etc.)
(1) The Special Prosecutor, Assistant Special Prosecutors, and Special Investigators (hereinafter referred to as the "Special Prosecutor, etc."), public officials seconded under Article 6 (4), and persons employed to assist the Special Prosecutor in the performance of duties shall not divulge secrets protected by statutes and regulations that they have learned in the course of their duties, either during service or after retirement.
(2) The Special Prosecutor, etc., public officials seconded under Article 6 (4), and persons employed to assist the Special Prosecutor in the performance of duties shall not publicly disclose or divulge the details of investigations, except in cases provided for in Article 9 (3) through (5), Article 11, and Article 12.
(3) Public officials seconded under Article 6 (4) shall not report to their home agencies information learned while performing their duties on secondment.
(4) The Special Prosecutor, etc. shall not engage in business for profit or concurrently hold other positions.
(5) The provisions concerning the duties of prosecutors in the Criminal Procedure Act, the Prosecutors' Office Act (excluding Article 4 (2)), the Military Court Act, and other statutes and regulations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Special Prosecutor and Assistant Special Prosecutors insofar as they do not conflict with this Act.

Article 9 (Investigation Periods, etc.)
(1) Within 20 days from the date of appointment, the Special Prosecutor may make preparations necessary for the performance of duties, including securing facilities necessary for investigations and requesting the appointment of Assistant Special Prosecutors: Provided, That even during the investigation preparation period, the Special Prosecutor may conduct relevant investigations where prompt collection of evidence is necessary to prevent its loss.
(2) The Special Prosecutor shall complete investigations of the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1) and decide whether to institute prosecution within 60 days beginning on the day following the date on which the preparation period under paragraph (1) expires.
(3) Where the Special Prosecutor is unable to complete an investigation or finds it difficult to decide whether to institute prosecution within the period under paragraph (2), the Special Prosecutor may extend the investigation period on no more than two occasions by 30 days each and shall report the reasons in writing to the President and the National Assembly. <Amended on September 26, 2025>
(4) Where, despite extensions of the investigation period under paragraph (3), the Special Prosecutor is unable to complete an investigation or finds it difficult to decide whether to institute prosecution within that period, the Special Prosecutor may report the reasons to the President and, with the President's approval, extend the investigation period once by 30 days.
(5) Reports and requests for approval under paragraphs (3) and (4) shall be made no later than three days before the investigation period expires, and, in cases under paragraph (4), the President shall notify the Special Prosecutor of whether approval is granted no later than the day preceding the expiration of the investigation period extended under paragraph (3). Where the President does not notify the Special Prosecutor of whether approval is granted, approval shall be deemed granted.
(6) Where the Special Prosecutor is unable to complete an investigation or decide whether to institute prosecution within the investigation period, the Special Prosecutor shall transfer the case to the head of the National Office of Investigation under Article 16 of the Act on the Organization and Operation of National Police and Autonomous Police within three days from the date the investigation period expires, in accordance with this Act, which shall take precedence over other Acts. In such cases, Article 17 shall apply mutatis mutandis to reports on expenditures, details of activities, etc., but the reporting period shall be calculated from the date the case is transferred. <Amended on September 26, 2025>
(7) A judicial police officer of the National Office of Investigation assigned a case under paragraph (6) shall promptly complete the investigation and, where grounds to suspect a crime are found, transfer the case without delay to the chief prosecutor of the district prosecutors' office having jurisdiction in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Act. <Amended on September 26, 2025>
(8) The chief prosecutor of the district prosecutors' office having jurisdiction who receives a case transferred under paragraph (7) shall decide whether to institute prosecution and take charge of the conduct of prosecution in cases in which prosecution has been instituted. In such cases, Article 11 shall apply mutatis mutandis to reports on the handling of the case. <Newly Inserted on September 26, 2025>

Article 10 (Trial Periods, etc.)
(1) Trials of cases in which the Special Prosecutor has instituted prosecution shall be conducted promptly and given priority over other trials, and judgments shall be pronounced within six months from the date of institution of prosecution at first instance and within three months from the date of pronouncement of the judgment in the preceding instance at each of the second and third instances.
(2) In cases under paragraph (1), the periods specified in Articles 361, 361-3 (1) and (3), 377, and 379 (1) and (4) of the Criminal Procedure Act shall each be seven days.
(3) Notwithstanding the proviso to Article 57 (1) of the Court Organization Act, hearings and judgments in trials concerning the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1) shall be open to the public. <Newly Inserted on September 26, 2025>
(4) Upon an application by the Special Prosecutor or the defendant, the presiding judge shall permit broadcasting unless there are special circumstances: Provided, That where the presiding judge determines that there are special circumstances warranting denial of permission to broadcast, the presiding judge may deny permission by a ruling and, in such cases, shall pronounce the ruling stating the reasons therefor. <Newly Inserted on September 26, 2025>
(5) In such trials, the entire hearing shall be recorded in shorthand by a stenographer and shall be audio-recorded or video-recorded (referring to video recording that includes audio recording) using an audio recording device or a video recording device. <Newly Inserted on September 26, 2025>
(6) Where a trial is broadcast under paragraph (4), de-identification measures for the contents of the trial, including personal information, private life, and State secrets (meaning visual or auditory measures to protect the personal safety or privacy of trial participants in the courtroom), need not be taken, and relevant public officials shall not incur civil or criminal liability in connection with such broadcasting unless it arises from intent or gross negligence. <Newly Inserted on September 26, 2025>

Article 11 (Reports on the Disposition of Cases) Where the Special Prosecutor decides not to institute prosecution or institutes prosecution in any of the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1), or where a judgment in such a case becomes final and conclusive, the Special Prosecutor shall report each such event in writing to the President and the National Assembly within 10 days.

Article 12 (Reports to the Public on Cases) The Special Prosecutor or an Assistant Special Prosecutor acting upon the Special Prosecutor's instructions may conduct press briefings on the course of an investigation, excluding the facts of the suspected offense, in relation to the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1), to guarantee the public's right to know.

Article 13 (Remuneration, etc.)
(1) The remuneration and treatment of the Special Prosecutor shall follow those of a chief prosecutor of a high prosecutors' office.
(2) The remuneration and treatment of an Assistant Special Prosecutor shall follow those of a chief prosecutor.
(3) The remuneration and treatment of a Special Investigator shall follow those of a State public official in special service equivalent to Grade III through Grade V.
(4) The Government shall pay from reserve funds the expenses necessary for the performance of the duties of the Special Prosecutor, etc. until the Special Prosecutor retires.
(5) The Special Prosecutor may request the State or public institutions to provide office space and equipment, including communications facilities, necessary for the performance of the duties of the Special Prosecutor, etc. In such cases, an institution receiving such a request shall comply with it unless there are justifiable grounds for not doing so.

Article 14 (Retirement, etc.)
(1) The Special Prosecutor shall not retire without justifiable grounds, and any request to retire shall be made in writing.
(2) Where the Special Prosecutor dies or submits a letter of resignation under paragraph (1), the President shall notify the National Assembly without delay and appoint a successor Special Prosecutor in accordance with the appointment procedures under Article 3 (2) through (5). In such cases, the successor Special Prosecutor shall succeed to the duties of the predecessor Special Prosecutor.
(3) Where a successor Special Prosecutor is appointed under paragraph (2), the investigation periods of the predecessor and successor Special Prosecutors shall be aggregated in calculating the investigation period under Article 9; however, the period from the date on which the Special Prosecutor submits a letter of resignation to the date on which the successor Special Prosecutor is appointed shall not be included in the investigation period.
(4) The Special Prosecutor, etc. shall automatically retire when a report has been submitted under Article 11 following a decision not to institute prosecution or a judgment becoming final and conclusive.

Article 15 (Dismissal, etc.)
(1) The President shall not dismiss the Special Prosecutor or an Assistant Special Prosecutor except in any of the following cases:
1. Where a ground for disqualification specified in any subparagraph of Article 4 is discovered;
2. Where the Special Prosecutor requests the President to dismiss an Assistant Special Prosecutor, deeming it necessary for the performance of duties or pursuant to Article 7 (6);
3. Where Article 8 (1) or (4) has been violated;
4. Where a provision concerning the duties of prosecutors that applies mutatis mutandis to the Special Prosecutor and Assistant Special Prosecutors pursuant to Article 8 (5) has been violated.
(2) Where the President dismisses the Special Prosecutor, the President shall notify the National Assembly without delay and appoint a successor Special Prosecutor in accordance with the appointment procedures under Article 3 (2) through (5). In such cases, the latter sentence of Article 14 (2) shall apply mutatis mutandis to succession to duties, and paragraph (3) of that Article shall apply mutatis mutandis to calculation of the investigation period.
(3) Where an Assistant Special Prosecutor dies or the President dismisses an Assistant Special Prosecutor, the President shall appoint a successor Assistant Special Prosecutor without delay pursuant to Article 7 (1). Provided, That this shall not apply where an Assistant Special Prosecutor is dismissed pursuant to paragraph (1) 2 (limited to cases under Article 7 (6)).
(4) Where necessary for the performance of duties, the Special Prosecutor may dismiss a Special Investigator or request the head of the relevant agency to replace a seconded public official belonging to that agency.

Article 16 (Security of Tenure) The Special Prosecutor and Assistant Special Prosecutors shall not be removed from office unless impeached or sentenced to imprisonment without labor or a more severe punishment.

Article 17 (Accounting Reports, etc.) Where the Special Prosecutor decides not to institute prosecution or a judgment in a case in which prosecution has been instituted becomes final and conclusive, the Special Prosecutor shall, within 10 days, report in writing to the President matters concerning expenditures, details of activities, etc., and transfer documents, etc. relating to duties that are in the Special Prosecutor's custody to the Prosecutor General. Provided, That, where prosecution has been instituted, the Special Prosecutor shall submit an interim report in writing to the President within 10 days on matters concerning expenditures, details of activities, etc. up to the date of institution of prosecution.

Article 18 (Judicial Authority and Jurisdiction)
(1) Notwithstanding the Military Court Act, courts shall have judicial authority over cases in which the Special Prosecutor has instituted prosecution pursuant to this Act and cases transferred to the Special Prosecutor for the conduct of prosecution.
(2) A collegiate division of the Seoul Central District Court shall have exclusive jurisdiction over trials of first instance in cases in which the Special Prosecutor has instituted prosecution pursuant to this Act.

Article 19 (Objections)
(1) A person who has become subject to investigation in a case specified in any subparagraph of Article 2 (1), or that person's spouse, lineal ascendant or descendant, cohabitant, or defense counsel, may file an objection with the Seoul High Court against acts of the Special Prosecutor exceeding the scope of duties, including a violation of Article 6 (2).
(2) An objection under paragraph (1) shall be filed in writing stating the grounds and shall be submitted through the Special Prosecutor.
(3) The Special Prosecutor receiving a written objection under paragraph (2) shall handle it as follows:
1. Where the Special Prosecutor finds the objection well-founded, the Special Prosecutor shall immediately take corrective measures in accordance with the objection and notify the Seoul High Court and the objector thereof in writing;
2. Where the Special Prosecutor finds the objection unfounded, the Special Prosecutor shall attach a written opinion to the written objection and forward it to the Seoul High Court within 24 hours from its receipt.
(4) The Seoul High Court receiving a written objection forwarded under paragraph (3) 2 shall decide on it as follows within 48 hours from its receipt. In such cases, the Court may, where necessary, examine evidence, including by inspecting investigation records:
1. Where the Court finds the objection unfounded, it shall dismiss the objection;
2. Where the Court finds the objection well-founded, it shall uphold the objection, recognizing that the matters under investigation challenged by the objection fall outside the scope of the Special Prosecutor's duties.
(5) Where a decision upholding an objection is rendered under paragraph (4) 2, the Special Prosecutor shall not engage in investigative activities contrary to the purport of that decision.
(6) No appeal may be filed against a decision under paragraph (4).
(7) The investigative activities of the Special Prosecutor shall not be suspended by the filing of an objection under paragraph (1).
(8) An objector under paragraph (1) may, concurrently with or separately from the objection, apply to the Seoul High Court, in writing substantiating the grounds, for suspension, in whole or in part, of the effect of the relevant disposition, etc., its execution, or the continuation of proceedings, and the Court shall decide on the application without delay.
(9) Where the Seoul High Court renders a decision under paragraph (4) or (8), it shall notify the objector and the Special Prosecutor in writing.

Article 20 (Penalty Provisions)
A person who obstructs the performance of duties by the Special Prosecutor, etc. by fraudulent means or force shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than five years.

Article 21 (Penalty Provisions)
(1) Where the Special Prosecutor, etc., a public official seconded under Article 6 (4), or a person employed to assist the Special Prosecutor in performing his or her duties discloses a secret protected under statutes or regulations that he or she has learned in the course of duties, in violation of Article 8 (1), such person shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than three years, suspension of qualifications for not more than five years, or a fine not exceeding 30 million won.
(2) Where the Special Prosecutor, etc., a public official seconded under Article 6 (4), or a person employed to assist the Special Prosecutor in performing his or her duties makes public or discloses the contents of an investigation in violation of Article 8 (2), such person shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than three years, suspension of qualifications for not more than five years, or a fine not exceeding 30 million won.
(3) Where a public official seconded under Article 6 (4) reports information learned in the course of performing duties to his or her home agency in violation of Article 8 (3), such person shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than three years, suspension of qualifications for not more than five years, or a fine not exceeding 30 million won.

Article 22 (Deeming Persons Public Officials for Purposes of Applying Penalty Provisions)
The Special Prosecutor, etc. and persons employed to assist the Special Prosecutor in performing his or her duties shall be deemed public officials for purposes of applying penalty provisions under the Criminal Act or other Acts.

Article 23 (Mitigation or Remission of Punishment, etc.)
Where a person who has violated the Criminal Act or another Act in connection with a case specified in any subparagraph of Article 2 (1) falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the punishment may be mitigated or remitted: Provided, That the punishment shall be mitigated or remitted in a case falling under subparagraph 1 or 3:
1. Where the person voluntarily surrenders after committing an offense under this Act;
2. Where a person who has committed an offense under this Act files an accusation against another person who has committed an offense under this Act or prevents another person from committing an offense under this Act;
3. Where the person is punished for his or her own offense in connection with making a material statement or giving material testimony that establishes another person's crime concerning the case during investigation or trial proceedings, submitting other materials, or providing information for the apprehension of an offender.

ADDENDA <Act No. 20989, June 10, 2025>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Period of Validity)
This Act shall remain in force until the date on which the Special Prosecutor retires pursuant to Article 14 (4): Provided, That Article 9 (8) shall remain in force until the date on which the chief prosecutor of the competent district prosecutors' office submits the report. <Amended on September 26, 2025>

Article 3 (Special Cases concerning Effects of Expiration)
The expiration of this Act shall not affect the penalty provisions under Articles 20 through 22.

Article 4 (Suspension of Statute of Limitations for Prosecution)
The statute of limitations for prosecution of the cases specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 (1) shall be deemed suspended from the date this Act is promulgated until the date the investigation period under Article 9 ends.

ADDENDA <Act No. 21063, September 26, 2025>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (General Applicability)
The amended provisions of this Act shall also apply, in relation to investigations ongoing at the time this Act enters into force by the Special Prosecutor to ascertain the truth concerning obstruction of the investigation into a Marine's death in the line of duty and concealment of the case, etc., to the matters subject to investigation, etc., the scope of duties and powers, etc. of the Special Prosecutor, Assistant Special Prosecutors and Special Investigators, investigation periods, etc., and the numbers of seconded prosecutors and seconded public officials, etc.

Article 3 (Applicability concerning Mitigation or Remission of Punishment, etc.)
The amended provisions of Article 23 shall also apply to cases under investigation or pending before a court at the time this Act enters into force.

All paragraphs, subparagraphs, provisos, amendment and insertion dates, references, and penalty provisions in the supplied source have been retained.
